description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare http_compatibility_bindings or unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. kind=branched declares a semantic request discriminator plus a closed effect_branches[] list with unique equals values and one final otherwise branch; each branch contains a complete event_log, actor_private_event, or none leaf effect. An event_log branch that is not unconditional MUST additionally name event_submission_path pointing to the caller-signed EventInitialSubmission used by that branch. Field presence is evidence carried by a branch, never the branch discriminator itself. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

delivery_authentication_record.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method and key digest; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id; registration_epoch is the effective destination Applet registration.
delivery_authentication_record.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare full_id MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. The effective registration_epoch and actual verification key digest are bound. Direct full-DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.
delivery_authentication_record.equality: Receivers recompute sha256(UTF8(digest_domain + newline) || RFC8785_JCS(record)); equal recomputed digests define replay equality. Caller-supplied records or digests are forbidden.

did_authority.purpose: Verify the announce governance proof of the announcing service or organization, and resolve the principal server endpoint inside the same first-ingest admission.
Verify the appellant governance signature on a takedown appeal packet before the Directory issues a decision receipt.

operations.notes: Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

did_authority.purpose: Verify the withdraw governance signature of the service or organization that owns the directory entry.

operations.notes: Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether the issuer ledger considers it active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The Account Authority MUST read the same issuer ledger used by issue, refresh, revoke and cascade; lifecycle status distinguishes active, revoked, superseded and dynamically expired records rather than consulting a Principal Event/cell. Introspection does not call back to the origin Principal Server and carries no reusable revocation-gate receipt: before accepting each protected self request, that origin Principal Server checks its own exact device/generation pending/Seal state locally in the request transaction. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority S2S producer operation for Native Agent signer evidence. The request carries agent_authority_service_resolution: the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord, adapter-discriminated method evidence and authenticated normalized DID Document. The receiver independently validates method evidence, document digest, record proof/currentness, project(full_id), and active assertion key before verifying an RFC 9421 signature that covers method, target URI/path, Content-Digest, Source/Destination-Service-ID, operation id and request id. A did_core_id, URL, bearer or caller-supplied public key is never the verification key source; bearer may only be an additional deployment gate. The authenticated source service MUST equal request.agent_authority_service_id and MUST byte-match service_id in request.principal_id's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding; that Principal Server is the Agent PCR authority under the managed-Agent same-server invariant. Ordinary clients and a caller-supplied account identity are forbidden. The Account Authority reads its own authoritative account binding/status projection, selects account_binding_default or account_status_event basis, and signs the closed controller_account_gate_attestation under domain ak.controller-account-gate-v1. issued_at <= expires_at and expires_at-issued_at MUST be <=300s. Unknown principal, missing current service binding, wrong source service and unauthorized caller are indistinguishable not_found outcomes and disclose no account status. Exact request_id plus canonical intent replay returns the byte-identical outcome while retained; same request_id with different principal or service is duplicate_conflict with zero issuance. The attestation is intentionally a reusable short-TTL controller-lifecycle snapshot and omits operation, request_digest, audience and challenge: per-request current_observation and outer_attestation bind its digest to those exact values, so a bare gate replay cannot validate another request. account_id and raw account cells never enter the request, outcome, logs visible to the caller or portable evidence.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED full_id to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus full_id rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve full_id itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(full_id)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Principal Server co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, full_id, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Issue a single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.2). Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header, and by nothing else: the PCR was never accepted, so the holder has no principal and therefore no principal-bound ak.session.grant. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, requires principal_id and did_version_id to equal the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that PCR is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, the abandoned principal_id, did_version_id, lease id and fence, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from ordinary login, session resume, lease fence advance or any automated flow.

Consume an identity-abandonment challenge and explicitly abandon the provisional identity. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header; the presented handoff MUST be a fresh one and MUST NOT be the grant that was presented when the challenge was issued. Whether that fresh handoff required re-authentication, which risk checks ran and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified. One transaction consumes the challenge, records the orphan anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppresses the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and releases the identity-creation lease; any step failing means zero writes. If the PCR was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with identity_creation_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because removing an established identity is the account deletion path. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The abandoned entry 0 stays a permanently unusable orphan anchor; its later handling is deployment governance.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger session-grant exchange. Before issuer commit, the Account Authority MUST obtain a fresh allow receipt from ak.peer.device_revocations.command.check for the exact device and immutable grant intent, and MUST copy that receipt's derived authorization Event and generation verbatim into the grant device_binding; a first ordinary human issuance sends no expected binding and acquires it from the receipt, while recovery completion and refresh MUST send their own verified durable binding and fail closed on generation_mismatch. The request carries device_id only, and a client-supplied authorization Event or generation MUST NOT be accepted. Human issuance always runs the gate and branches three ways: allow issues the bound grant, authority_mismatch means the device has no accepted authorization yet and MAY issue only the fresh-device restricted grant scoped to ak.key.verification.* bootstrap with no device_binding, and revocation_pending, revoked or generation_mismatch issue nothing and never degrade into that restricted grant. revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and no grant record/JWT. After validating account-to-principal binding, authentication proof, holder DPoP, audience and scope ceiling, the issuer uses the proof-specific stable request identity and canonical intent digest to atomically persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. The grant ID and JWT jti are recomputed from that record under id_kind_registry.issuer_record_identity_contract; no Principal Event is authored. Exact replay revalidates holder/DPoP/target/digest and returns the byte-identical recorded outcome. Same request identity with different canonical intent is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. A replay whose outcome is expired or revoked/superseded returns the registered terminal error and never issues a replacement; an evicted replay record fails closed as indeterminate. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome and the client presents ak.session.grant directly to /_arkret/self/* with DPoP. For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges and validates the code. For proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff, the DPoP-bound handoff account MUST already be bound to principal_id. The Account Authority never derives a principal DID from OIDC and never obtains or uses a principal/root/device/notary Event-signing key.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Final native Agent runtime-key authorization. The closed Ed25519 possession proof MUST be byte-identical to the current persisted runtime request and still fresh; the authority rebuilds its server-record-bound transcript, stable runtime binding and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1 (including current proof digest) before accepting the controller-signed authorize Event. A stale prompt or any body/record/evidence mismatch fails closed without consuming the pairing handle.

Authorizes a sibling device only after verified current-device confirmation. This operation always produces authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, so device_signature MUST verify under ak.device-authorize-accepted-device-possession-proof-v1 and registration_anchor/pcr_recovery domains MUST be rejected. The authority recomputes the pairing transcript, verifies exact request/Event equality and submits the current-device-signed Event through ordinary PCR admission; it never resolves current human DID authority.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantIntent; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger session-grant rotation. Before successor commit, the issuer MUST obtain a fresh exact-intent allow receipt from ak.peer.device_revocations.command.check; pending/revoked blocks refresh even when the predecessor grant and DPoP are otherwise valid. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). Exact replay revalidates current holder/DPoP and returns the recorded successor outcome; conflicting canonical bytes are duplicate_conflict. One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves the independently allocated session_id, and atomically marks the predecessor superseded with successor_session_grant_id. A replay whose recorded successor is expired or revoked/superseded returns the registered terminal error and never issues another successor. Account Authority-local op; no Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer full_id and principal_id; every repeated full_id/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified full_id, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, full_id, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_arkret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

Account Authority exchanges an OIDC authorization code for an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key and returns the deployment-local stable account_subject. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, issue_identity_abandonment_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. The two abandonment operations are on that list because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can exist to carry them. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy state and atomically acquires, renews, or fences a rate-limited identity-creation lease for the authenticated service account. Busy includes the conflicting live lease expires_at without holder identity. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. A different holder cannot take an unexpired lease; after expiry, a newly authenticated holder may fence it and must preserve all frozen checkpoints.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The closed Ed25519 proof binds the local key to the authoritative pairing handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, authority service DID, stable runtime binding and no-more-than-five-minute window; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize bound to the current proof digest. Pairing secret and proof MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and atomically replace the current freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the current public principal resolution projection from the known Principal Server. The response carries only the account pair, the projection, bounded adapter method evidence and the Principal Server projection attestation; it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted Seal. Account-internal audit material moved to ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit, so this surface has no history selector. This is a second-hop projection fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, verify the attestation proof under the current principal_server_id method history, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(full_id)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Returns the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord at the stable current_record_url carried by bootstrap material. TLS is transport only. Consumers verify the record proof, method history, project(full_id)=service_id, time ordering, record_sequence/previous_record_digest and describe binding. Same-core successors refresh route caches without Realm rebind; a changed did_core_id requires a new authorized service binding.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventInitialSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through ordinary Event admission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

discriminator.description: The caller-declared semantic MIMI update kind. The decoded opaque payload MUST carry the same kind before a branch is admitted.

operations.notes: Account Authority or authorized Principal Server publication of exactly one ak.account.status Event into the account principal's Principal Control Realm. The caller uses service-to-service HTTP Message Signature authentication and a required Idempotency-Key covered by the signature. authority_evidence is Account Authority-signed transport evidence binding account_id, principal_id, principal_control_realm_id, issuer service and a live authority_ref; the receiver independently verifies it, the Event proof, exact Event/evidence field equality, current issuer key/delegation and PCR CBA closure. Initial publication carries the Event without an AuthorizationLease; downstream fanout adds receiver-signed account_status_receipts and CbaProofBundle values. AccountStatusReceipt proves local frontier acceptance, contains no AuthorizationLease id, and generic IngressReceipt is forbidden. Same key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict. A byte-identical retry returns the latest durable operation state, allowing pending_seal and fanout progress to converge without creating another Event. accepted or duplicate is terminal for the receiving server's frontier; multi-server propagation continues from a durable bounded outbox and never mutates the signed account-status payload.

Read-only service-authenticated Account Authority query for the exact issuer actor-chain frontier and Principal Control Realm Seal frontier needed to sign one ak.account.status Event. The receiver verifies the signed authority_evidence, current issuer delegation and account/principal/PCR binding before disclosure. The response binds RealmActorFrontierView.actor_id to issuer_service_id and both frontier realm_id values to principal_control_realm_id; it grants no authority, accepts no Event and never synthesizes an empty PCR.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, or tombstone facts plus their exact source acceptance receipts and refreshable current proof. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events. Branches use byte-identical durable replay; the receiver never re-signs or treats tentative/stale evidence as authority.

Service-authenticated relay for an exact requester-authorized ak.member.repair.request. The source copies request_id, content and detached requester authorization byte for byte from the accepted self dispatch, appends exactly one portable device or Native Agent current-authority evidence branch, and covers the complete body with Content-Digest and RFC 9421. The destination independently binds requester identity, accepted rejoin actor and subject, authorization Event, current evidence and exact requester_keypackage_ref signer. In one transaction keyed by (Source-Service-ID, request_id), it freezes request_digest, resolves the peer participant from the accepted Direct Conversation binding, and atomically chooses one closed recipient branch: snapshot every currently authorized human device and enqueue all stable distinct message ids, or enqueue one stable message id to the Native Agent's current active runtime endpoint from accepted agent-key/session binding. Exact replay returns the stored byte-identical outcome; a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Success proves only durable enqueue, never business repair acceptance.

Service-authenticated hard-erasure receipt fanout. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. Idempotency-Key is required and covered by the HTTP Message Signature; its scope is (source service, destination service, key). The receiver verifies the closed receipt, issuer authority at receipt.issued_at, every receipt proof, receipt_digest and the exact retained-stub binding before any deletion or durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. An accepted or duplicate acknowledgement closes the sender outbox item.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response. The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.

Authenticated Account-Authority-to-origin-Principal-Server revocation gate, binding source and issuance fence. The request binds the exact PrincipalAuthorityKey, device, action class and immutable issuer intent digest; the authorization Event and PCR-local generation are derived by the origin from its own durable current device projection inside the gate transaction, under the same rule ak.device.revoke uses, and are never taken from the request or from client input. expected_device_authorize_event_id and expected_device_generation_ref are the issuer's own verified durable binding, appear together or not at all, MAY be omitted only for session_grant_issue, and are required for every other action class. The origin service authenticates the caller and confirms it is the Account Authority bound to that exact pair before any private device lookup, then atomically linearizes the request against its durable accepted revoke proposal/decision/Seal log and persists a signed decision receipt. A validated request always returns the typed 200 receipt (allow, revocation_pending, revoked, authority_mismatch or generation_mismatch); 409 gate errors belong to the blocked business operation. Only allow carries the derived target_device_authorize_event_id and target_device_generation_ref, and that pair is the sole source for the issued grant device_binding; withholding it from generation_mismatch is what stops a refresh from silently re-issuing at a replaced generation. An unauthorized caller, an account this service does not host, an unknown device and a device outside the named account are indistinguishable authority_mismatch. An allow receipt admits only those exact immutable bytes before any later revocation_pending transition; exact replay returns the byte-identical receipt. Receipt expiry is at most 30 seconds and is only a use-freshness bound; cache state is never authoritative. Session-grant issue/refresh MUST hold the matching fresh receipt. Introspection carries no reusable receipt; the origin Principal Server gates every protected self request locally in its request transaction.

Federation peer Event publication. Each EventFederationSubmission carries the original signed Event. Ordinary online publication omits AuthorizationLease and uses an empty ingress_receipts array; explicit delayed/offline publication carries the lease and at least one original lease-bound IngressReceipt. An ak.member.state compensation publication additionally carries the unchanged transport-only membership_compensation_evidence and the receiver applies the same exact admission/incarnation/action/executor/single-use evaluator as initial submission. Request-level CbaProofBundle values provide receiver-relative dependency closure. The receiver independently validates every Event, optional lease, receipt threshold, compensation evidence, bundle object and reducer result. Ordinary missing dependencies use HTTP 200 partial items with reason_code=dependency_missing and non-empty typed missing sets; registered atomic units use top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with EventsDependencyMissingProblem and zero writes. A received response terminates that Idempotency-Key; a post-backfill submit uses a fresh key. The caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim remains decided by the destination Realm reducer. The request union additionally registers the discriminated direct_conversation_founding branch for the Direct Conversation founding exception of zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4: it carries exactly four ordered EventFederationSubmission items (Realm create, peer membership join, main Strand create, founder membership join), the source DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceReceipt and bounded dependencies, and it omits service_binding_ref because the Realm does not yet exist at the receiver. The receiver freshly verifies transport source authority over founder_id, cutover/fence continuity when the receipt came from a pre-migration service, destination binding to the local participant, body closure, recomputed founding_unit_digest and coordinates, and the full direct_conversation_genesis admission before admitting the unit at one atomic boundary. The agent_membership_cascade branch preserves the origin-signed controller terminal Event and Agent transitions and applies the same exact controller pair/generation, pre-state exact-set, signer and atomicity rules as self submission. A missing dependency for either registered unit is a retryable top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes, never a per-item partial and never a permanent rejection.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Read-only federation dependency resolution for canonical-bytewise sorted exact Event IDs, Event digests, and Seal refs in one Realm. Returns visible Events and receiver-relative CbaProofBundle values under a caller-selected response budget capped at 8 MiB. It never accepts an Event or Seal and never advances a frontier. Every selector is fully accounted for by a returned object or an indistinguishable same-type missing entry; if complete accounting cannot fit the budget, the whole operation returns limit_exceeded rather than a partial success.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.read.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Authenticated client dispatch of private invite evidence through the inviter Principal Server. The carried invite Event must already be accepted by this service, be authored by the current session actor, and match the stored canonical Event bytes exactly. Local delivery reuses the peer receive policy path; remote delivery enters the exact-body durable S2S outbox without re-authoring the Event.

Atomic cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim. The destination Principal Server is the sole CAS authority. The authenticated source Principal Server first admits the participant request against its exact local account/device/generation durable state; revocation_pending fails before any remote call or inventory disclosure and is exposed only as the existing opaque claim_failed result. Request and response carry no PCR/control-history or signer-evidence sidecar. Every claim binds the matching accepted authorization Event id, whose in-envelope Principal Server admission proof, the signed destination claim receipt, exact selectors and KeyPackage signature MUST all validate. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and the canonical request digest.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Account Authority transparently relays the exact client-signed PCR genesis unit after authenticating the service account and freezing the account/principal reservation. The outer service signature is transport authentication only. Principal admission independently validates the DID inception root, identity_creation_control_proof, the event-derived PCR id retype(create.event_id) which is never derived from the principal DID or subject and is never server-chosen, empty frontier, ordered root-signed create plus founding-device-signed authorize, single-direction payload digest binding, lease fence and expiry. Acceptance is atomic and create-once at the account dimension: two genesis attempts produce two different realm_id values, so implementations MUST NOT detect concurrency by id equality. Exact replay returns the original pcr_genesis_unit receipt and a conflicting unit performs zero writes.

Realm-scoped service-authenticated publication of exactly one target-signed ServiceResolutionRecord or ServiceRouteHandoverNotice. Idempotency-Key is required, is covered by the HTTP Message Signature, and MUST equal body.request_id. Transport replay is keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, request_id) and binds the complete canonical request digest: exact replay returns the original ack and a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Artifact integrity is independently keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, target service_id, artifact family/key/revision): the same artifact key with another digest conflicts with zero overwrite. The receiver validates source peer authority, target visibility, exact artifact_digest, target proof, full_id-to-core projection, sequential record/notice basis, time rules and hard bounds before writing its service-local mirror ledger. The receiver-signed ack cross-binds both keys, request_digest and accepted time; it proves durable receipt of exact bytes only and never makes a URL authoritative or declares a migration safe unless the deployment-required peer set has all acked.

Read-only Realm-scoped recovery of at most 32 continuous target-signed successor records and one active target-signed handover notice within a caller-selected response budget capped at 256 KiB. The authenticated requester must be a current allowed federation peer and must already be authorized to know the target service core through an effective joined-member delivery binding or explicit service delegation. Unknown, unauthorized, invisible, not-held and unavailable are outwardly indistinguishable and query/source/target rate limits prevent enumeration. The responder never returns a mirror-signed bare URL. The requester independently verifies every target proof, exact chain, freshness, method history and describe reverse binding; same sequence with different valid target-signed digests enters route-fork quarantine rather than majority, arrival-order or reachability selection.

Optional Signal Extension single-hop peer relay. The source batches original producer-signed encrypted SignalEnvelope values for one Realm and one destination service. The destination independently verifies peer authentication, current delivery binding, envelope proof, scope, Seal, signal_class, TTL and encrypted payload binding, then performs only local live fanout. The request MUST NOT carry Idempotency-Key; uncertain outcomes use drop_unconfirmed. The opaque accepted=true response reveals no Realm, scope, sender, recipient, binding, support, or per-signal result and is not a durable delivery receipt.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

The wrapper carries one complete DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id plus the current published full_id; the receiver independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The referenced challenge MUST bind both identifiers, local_admin_subject and the requested scope set, and the method-native control transcript MUST bind organization_id, full_id, the pinned version_id/log_head_digest and that challenge context. The outcome and signed receipt echo both identifiers; the receipt also binds version_id and control_key_digest so the accepted control state remains auditable. Creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. Idempotency is per generation: replaying the current generation's byte-identical request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. This operation registers a reference and local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, make this deployment the controller, or create Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external, already-published Organization DID. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published full_id; before issuing the challenge the registry independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The response challenge echoes and binds both identifiers together with purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, requested scopes, beneficiary local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds. Two phases are mandatory: the registry remembers this challenge, then ensure supplies a method-native proof over the same control transcript. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, defeating freshness and single use. The challenge MUST be consumed on first successful use. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, and the caller MUST prove against the newest challenge.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. The request MUST carry stable organization_id as did_core_id and the current published full_id; the receiver independently resolves and validates full_id with the registered method adapter and requires project(full_id)=organization_id. The fresh challenge and method-native control transcript bind both identifiers plus the refreshed version_id/log_head_digest. The refreshed outcome and signed receipt echo organization_id and full_id and bind version_id and control_key_digest. A same-core full_id refresh updates resolution/control state, not identity. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control after controller rotation and a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id only, returning the current binding outcome with a receipt whose status=revoked and created=false. No full_id is required because revoke addresses the already-bound local identity rather than resolving or proving fresh external control. This local act does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history. revoked is terminal for the generation; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with full_id, a new challenge and a new control proof.

Read the local binding by stable organization_id did_core_id without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. The outcome includes the current published full_id and signed receipt, with project(full_id)=organization_id and receipt/control-state bindings defined by OrganizationRegistrationOutcome and OrganizationRegistrationReceipt. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventInitialSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control Seal MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before Seal materialization it returns retry-safe frontier_unavailable for the same Event id.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

did_authority.when: proof_kind == did_root and the accepted PCR recovery policy explicitly enables the factor

operations.notes: Idempotently return or create the service identity bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base) registration key. The client supplies full_id plus the client-controlled signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof, requires state.id=full_id, projects full_id to the returned service_id did_core_id, and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base) key without creating or mutating identity state.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Carries exactly one holder-signed profile_event EventInitialSubmission and no unsigned patch. event.realm_id is the exact account-local PCR Realm selector; accepted-profile presence is evaluated only in that PCR lineage. If it has no accepted Actor Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.create; its actor_profile ID is derived by retyping the create Event ID and payload.object must omit id. If it has an accepted Profile, the Event must be ak.profile.update, payload.target_ref must equal that create-derived ID, and the signed patch remains limited to display_name, avatar_blob_ref and profile_fields.<key>. Both branches bind realm scope to the same PCR and event.actor_id to the session principal. On create payload.object.principal_id must equal that principal; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id must equal it. Direct holder proof is required without executor or Applet provenance. Event preconditions are empty; update concurrency uses only optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service forwards the exact bytes through ordinary Event admission without authoring, rebuilding, co-signing, choosing an ID or adding a concurrency guard. Until the Control Move has accepted Seal coverage the operation returns frontier_unavailable; exact retry after coverage returns the byte-identical stored outcome. The single accepted effect advances the holder account-aggregate projection once; it creates no Directory announcement or account-data Event.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. Because the operation has no account-local-lineage selector, profile is present only when exactly one accepted profile is unambiguous across the principal's PCR lineages; multiple accepted lineages fail closed by omitting profile, never by choosing an implicit current PCR. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, unread / notification counts). Signal envelopes use the Signal Extension live rail and are not account aggregate state. Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Submits the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event. The actor-private cell subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so only the holder may sign it and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. expected_revision is the Event payload's; it is no longer a query parameter. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused here.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_revision + 1. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Consume an agent-provisioning abandonment challenge and explicitly give up an accepted ak.agent.provision whose declared managed Agent PCR genesis will never be submitted (zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3). Authenticated by the controller user_session; the presented credentials MUST be fresh and MUST NOT be the ones presented when the challenge was issued, while re-authentication strength, risk checks and cooldown are deployment governance. One transaction consumes the challenge, releases the agent_slug selector claim and the principal_control_realm_id claim, records the tombstone / audit reservation and suppresses every holder-readable trace of the allocation; any step failing means zero writes. If the genesis was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with agent_pcr_genesis_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because an established Agent is retired through ak.self.agent.command.deactivate. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The accepted provision Event stays in the controller PCR history and the abandoned realm id MUST NOT be reused.

Issue the single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning an accepted ak.agent.provision whose declared managed Agent PCR genesis was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md section 3.6.3). Authenticated by the controller user_session. The service requires agent_id, principal_control_realm_id and allocation_handle to equal the authenticated controller's accepted provision, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that genesis is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to the controller account_subject, holder key, agent_id, agent_slug, the declared principal_control_realm_id, the allocation, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from lease expiry, garbage collection or any automated flow.

Controller-only caller-signed ak.capability.revoke Control Move. Path grant_id, payload grant_id/grant_ref, path Agent subject, target Realm, authenticated actor, the exact account-local lineage selected by the session, and the sole signed head_eq guard on the complete grant-cell head are all admission invariants. The service never authors the Event or appends CAS after signing; exact replay returns event.created_at as revoked_at.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus read-only owned/effective Agent sets, native MLS context and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope.

Only outward carrier for the PCR-resident ak.profile.create / ak.profile.update facts. A global profile Event lives in its owner's Principal Control Realm, so a co-member cannot reach it through a Realm-scoped read and MUST NOT reach it through a cross-principal actor selector on ak.self.events.read.scan. Authorization is current effective joined membership of body realm_id for both the caller and each returned actor; realm_id MUST NOT be a Principal Control Realm. Each row returns the exact signed profile Event and the accepted Seal covering that one event_digest, and never any other Event of that Realm. Unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, non-member actor and unauthorized caller all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot probe membership or account existence.

Closed selector XOR. current_admission binds the actual operation, request digest, verifier, audience and challenge and may authorize first live Signal evidence through current shared context. historical_event binds Event id, digest and receiver service and returns only the destination-signed admission receipt persisted when that exact Event was accepted; current state never reconstructs historical validity.

Read-only pre-admission of final signed Events followed by one authority-issued publication lease per Event. The operation never commits an Event or advances a frontier. Ordinary Events bind an accepted seal_ref/seal_basis; only complete registered genesis units may bind the ordered anchor_unit digest. Idempotent retry returns byte-identical leases.

Query parameters are realm_id, subject, required subject_principal_server_id and optional at. subject plus subject_principal_server_id form the exact PrincipalAuthorityKey; no local-service, bearer-service, DID-document or delivery-binding fallback is allowed.

Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend kinds (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is backend-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.archive Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active). The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event carried in create_event through ordinary Event admission; the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service MUST NOT mint it, and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.restore Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.tombstone Event carried in lifecycle_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.target_ref MUST name the path Circle. Terminal: the lifecycle matrix admits no transition out, so the signed Event is the whole record of who ended the Circle. Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission; payload.circle_id MUST equal the path circle_id. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event, nor add a capability verdict to the closed payload.

Submits the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event carried in member_event through ordinary Event admission. The Event membership MUST be leave and payload.expected_membership MUST carry the concrete current membership as its signed head_eq guard; payload.circle_id and payload.actor_id MUST equal the two path identifiers, and event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle. The service MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Control Move carried in grant_event through ordinary Event admission. payload.consent_id is the producer-allocated cell subject and the or_set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>', so the service chooses neither and MUST NOT synthesize the Event. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_principal_id defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell.

Submits the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Control Move carried in revoke_event through ordinary Event admission. Its payload.observed_dots MUST enumerate the active grant dots being removed for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope), read back from consent_cell_view.active_grant_dots. Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes and MUST still enumerate every dot; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST equal holder_principal_id or be an explicitly authorised holder controller; peers never receive this DTO.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted. Recontact may import one generic mutually signed bilateral prefix checkpoint plus at most 64 uncompressed tail rounds. Missing material is continuity_evidence_unavailable; invalid, rollback or forked material is continuity_invalid. A new lineage never inherits the old checkpoint, history or audit identity.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact round and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Holder contact projection from source-signed request/response receipts, issuer-local Contact lineages and current signed head leases. An accepted row also carries the closed next_prepare_input cursor whose contact_round_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update or ak.self.contact.command.tombstone; every other contact_state omits it, and the projected request/response/tombstone event refs are never authoritative lineage heads. A pending_incoming row likewise carries request_receipt, the complete signed request_acceptance_receipt copied verbatim into the prepare phase of ak.self.contact.command.respond or ak.self.contact.command.reject; it is signed by the peer's source service rather than by this server, so the client verifies it independently instead of trusting this server's retelling. Every other contact_state omits it, because pending_outgoing has no incoming request to answer and accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned have a consumed admission slot or a terminal round; a glare pair is never pending_incoming, so the glare ban on respond and reject needs no extra code. Private Consent and account-data notes are never Contact authority.

Issue one immutable current-authority authority Ack for a fully signed Control Move. Local device/Agent authorities use the same typed request and outcome without an HTTP hop. A caller canonically sorts distinct authority Acks and may submit the resulting receipt set only when the current notary profile quorum and common-window rules are satisfied.

Authenticated submission of one complete signed_defer or signed_reject. The receiver loads the durable accepted proposal and its immutable canonical ControlProposalAck, recomputes proposal_ack_digest, verifies the exact Realm/proposal/authority-set/deadline/defer chain and quorum, then atomically persists the decision. Exact decision replay is byte-identical duplicate; conflicting terminal or post-Seal decisions fail closed. For ak.device.revoke, only a valid signed_reject for the exact proposal/Ack (therefore the exact reducer-derived device and generation) clears that proposal's revocation_pending record; it clears no other pending revoke for the device.

Authenticated exact proposal observation surface. Returns only the durable authority discriminator, canonical Ack when applicable, verified decision chain and covering Seal state for the requested Realm/proposal digest. control_proposal_ack permits the closed pending/deferred/overdue/rejected/sealed chain and always carries Ack; the narrow ackless_event_proof branch permits only pending/sealed and carries no Ack, decision or Ack-derived deadline fault. ak.device.revoke is always control_proposal_ack. The operation cannot mint an Ack, synthesize a reject or mutate pending state; unauthorized and unknown selectors are non-enumerating.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with param_invalid (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. The sender's exact durable device/generation state is checked in the queue transaction; revocation_pending returns device_revocation_pending and enqueues nothing. Each target carries a sender-assigned message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates: a Direct Conversation Realm is created solely by the founder derived from the pair's root Contact round (normal branch takes the responder, glare branch takes the requests[0] issuer) through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.
